name: Bruck am Ziller
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny village right on the Ziller with a lakeside bath and perfect location between Fügen and Zell.
beschreibung:
Overview

Bruck am Ziller is a charming and peaceful municipality in the Schwaz district, located at an altitude of approximately 579 meters on a sunny terrace at the eastern gateway to the Zillertal. Home to around 1,120 residents, this sun-drenched village nestles at the foot of Mount Reither Kogel (1,336 m), comprising the main village, the hamlet of Imming on the valley floor, and scenic hillside farmsteads on the Bruckerberg. Situated away from the valley's busy main transit routes, Bruck offers tranquil seclusion, deep-rooted traditions, and an ideal setting connecting the Zillertal, the Alpbach Valley, and the Inn Valley, with wide-open views across the mountains.

History

Early medieval records document settlement here: the hamlet of Imming was mentioned as early as 976 as Himinga in Salzburg charters, while Bruck was first recorded in 1188 as villa Prukke. The name stems from the historic wooden bridge spanning the Ziller River, which for centuries served as the border between the County of Tyrol and the Archbishopric of Salzburg, hosting customs and judicial posts. During the 16th and 17th centuries, copper and silver mining flourished on the slopes of the Reither Kogel. The parish church dedicated to Saint Leonard was documented in 1337; its Gothic steeple dates to the 14th century, while the Baroque nave was expanded in 1738 by master builder Jakob Singer. An enormous Saint Christopher fresco from 1718 adorns the church exterior, and during Easter, the church displays an elaborate historic Holy Sepulchre with Baroque painted scenery.

How to Get There

Motorists reach Bruck via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Wiesing/Zillertal and following federal highway B169 to Strass im Zillertal, where provincial road L294 crosses the river into the village. Rail travelers take the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn from Jenbach to Schlitters-Bruck am Ziller station on the western riverbank, connected by a scenic fifteen-minute walk or local bus. Regional VVT bus route 633 stops regularly at the village square.

Tips

A rewarding hike leads up to the Spitzerköpfl viewpoint at 809 meters, crowned by a summit cross offering spectacular vistas of the Rofan range and the Zillertal entrance. Mountain enthusiasts can summit the Reither Kogel or traverse via the Kerschbaumersattel pass into the Alpbach Valley. For summer relaxation, Lake Schlitters (Schlitterer See), located just 1.5 kilometers away, offers swimming lawns and an adventure playground. Village inns serve authentic Zillertaler Krapfen filled with tangy grey cheese, while festive cattle drives and the Saint Leonard equestrian pageant in November showcase living Tyrolean heritage.
